Impact and mechanisms of lactylation in various cancers

The impact and mechanisms of lactylation in various cancers. Lactylation modification regulates gene expression and protein function through various signaling pathways, thereby promoting tumor progression in multiple cancer types. This figure illustrates the role of lactylation in different tumors, including (A) ocular melanoma, (B) hepatocellular carcinoma, (C) gastric cancer, (D) colorectal cancer, (E) clear cell renal cell carcinoma, (F) bladder carcinoma, (G) anaplastic thyroid cancer, (H) prostate cancer, (I) lung carcinoma, (J) breast cancer, and (K) endometrial carcinoma/cervical carcinoma. In each of these cancers, lactylation contributes to malignancy through distinct molecular mechanisms. Arrows indicate activation; bar‐headed lines indicate inhibition; up/down arrows indicate molecular upregulation or downregulation.
